g0.rationale: §2.2 five-step test run on the frozen directions. Step 1: authoritative directions located (aggregated, moderate-high confidence). Step 2, mode by mode — (a) mask mode 'Nach dem Waschen sanft auf das nasse Haar auftragen und 2 bis 3 Minuten einwirken lassen, gründlich ausspülen': after cleansing YES, stated contact time YES, rinse YES → qualifies; (b) Pre-Shampoo-Behandlung: not after cleansing → fails; (c) Spülung nach dem Shampoonieren: after cleansing and rinsed, but no stated contact time → fails §2.1's contact-time conjunct; (d) Leave-in: no rinse → fails. Step 3: exactly one mode qualifies → classify only that mode, record multi_use: true and name the uncovered modes. Charter F1 governs; the marketing name '4-in-1' never decides.

directions: 'Kann zusätzlich als Pre-Shampoo-Behandlung, als Spülung nach dem Shampoonieren, oder als Leave-in verwendet werden (4-in-1)'

tailMarker.anomalyNote: No §3.1 anomaly. The marker at 13 gives the cohort's second-longest above-tail segment and is what makes the gluconamide pair (@8/@9) qualifying here while the identical pair in #02 (ranks 11/12 against a marker at 8) is not. It also correctly demotes Amodimethicone @14, Butyrospermum Parkii Butter @15 and Prunus Armeniaca Kernel Oil @18 to decorative — the exact pattern lexicon §0.2 records for this product family.  ||  PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1, added under v0.2): PLAUSIBLE. The full care and weight architecture - CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4, DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE @5, ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @6, BEHENAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @7 - outranks PARFUM @13; conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA @1. Neither limb fires. SERICIN @12 sits at tail_index - 1: R3's tail-edge exclusion is scoped to §9.1's S1/S2/S3 and §9.2's base terms and does not reach §9.3's material-R5 test, so Sericin still counts there - recorded as a counter-signal on careDirection rather than silently relied on.  ||  RE-DERIVED UNDER v0.4 (E8, 2026-09-30): R3's tail-edge exclusion is NOT extended to §9.3's material-R5 test. Following E1's principle, SERICIN @12 (tail_index − 1) counts normally there; the boundary dependence is carried as the careDirection confidence cap at `moderate` and a `boundary_position_ingredient` hinweise note.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only, exact-market DE INCI of record (sha256 f5a2c0ca…), above-tail ranks 1–12; category-relative to the German drugstore rinse-out mask shelf.
conditioningLevel.rationale: All three §9.1 structural signals are satisfied, and the cationic leg is satisfied by three chemically distinct species rather than the minimum two. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, not measured treatment performance.
evidenceSignals: BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 4) — permanent long-chain quat
DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE (rank 5) — esterquat, a second distinct cationic species
BEHENAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE (rank 7) — protonatable amidoamine, a third distinct cationic species
CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three
ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE (rank 6) and GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS (rank 10) — two distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail
conditioningLevel.derivation: S1 satisfied (3 distinct cationics, against a required 2). S2 satisfied (Cetearyl Alcohol @2). S3 satisfied (Isopropyl Myristate @6 is a light ester and Glycosphingolipids @10 is a ceramide-class lipid, both named R4 candidate evidence). Count = 3 of 3.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `high`: ≥2 of {S1,S2,S3} with no material counter-signal; three independent families converge.
`moderate` does not apply: three signals are satisfied, not one or zero.
`low` does not apply: it requires none of the three.

Recorded for calibration: this is the only cohort formula where S1 is met by three distinct species, which is the exact pattern lexicon §15's C1 adjudication identified as the genuine outlier against a market baseline of one.

Re-derived under v0.2 (R3): the value `high` STANDS on the new rule. S1 is satisfied and survives the tail-edge exclusion — BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4, DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE @5 and BEHENAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @7 are three distinct cationic/amidoamine species, all ranked above tail_index − 1 (SERICIN @12). S2 is satisfied by CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, also clear of the band. S1 plus one of {S2, S3} with no material counter-signal is exactly R3's `high` anchor. The v0.1 'any 2 of 3' arithmetic this record cited is superseded; the value does not move because the signal R3 made mandatory is the one this formula has most of.
counterSignals: Ceteareth-20 @21 and Trideceth-10 @22 are tail-position silicone/fragrance solubilisers — normal and meaningless (lexicon family 10).
S3's second member, Glycosphingolipids @10, is a trace-level lipid; §11's weak-evidence marking W4 applies, so the S3 leg is the softest of the three.
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support.
Single fallback-tier source; both preferred retailers were unreachable.

evidenceSignals: BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (4), DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE (5), BEHENAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE (7) — required base leg 1, met three times over
CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — required base leg 2, met
BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER (rank 15) — R4b heavy lipid, but BELOW tail_index 13
PRUNUS ARMENIACA KERNEL OIL (rank 18) — mid lipid, below the marker
AMODIMETHICONE (rank 14) — the formula's only silicone, below the marker; no second silicone species anywhere
ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE (rank 6) — a light ester, explicitly not R4b
claims 'ölfrei', 'ohne Mineralöle' — consistent with the credited architecture
weightPotential.derivation: §9.2 required base met. Alternative (a) an R4b heavy lipid above the tail: NOT met — the butter is at 15, two ranks below the marker. Alternative (b) an occlusive silicone stack above the tail (two or more silicone species, or a dimethicone/dimethiconol pair): NOT met — one silicone, in the tail. With base met but neither alternative, the anchor fails.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moderate`: §9.2 assigns `moderate` to everything the `high` anchor and the `low` anchor do not capture, and explicitly calls it the expected majority.
`high` does not apply: the base-plus-one-alternative structure Nick ruled on 2026-09-04 requires at least one supporting route, and both candidates sit below the tail marker where they earn nothing.
`low` does not apply: it requires a single cationic species (there are three) and no cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three (Cetearyl Alcohol is at 2).
Confirms the intended behaviour of §9.2's counter-signal rules: a 'Bonding/Silk' mask that lists shea butter on pack does not become heavy because of it.

Re-derived under v0.2 (R4): the value `moderate` STANDS, and both anchors now fail for stated reasons rather than for want of a cationic count. `high` fails on its required core: there is no R4b heavy lipid above the marker at all — ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @6 is a light ester, GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS @10 is a trace family-11 species, and BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER @15 and PRUNUS ARMENIACA KERNEL OIL @18 are both tail-side and decorative, exactly the pattern lexicon §0.2 records for this product family. `low` fails on the thin-fatty-base conjunct: CETEARYL ALCOHOL sits at rank 2, inside the top three. Residual = `moderate`.

Re-checked under v0.3/v0.4 (E4, E7): value `moderate` STANDS, and the `low` refusal now rests on the restated leanness test rather than on the deleted thin-fatty-base conjunct cited above — conjunct 3 fails on THREE cationics (BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4, DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE @5, BEHENAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @7), which is the same count on the above-tail segment and on the full list (E7).
counterSignals: Front-of-pack lipid storytelling versus tail-position lipids — the lexicon's canonical false positive for this exact product family.
Single fallback-tier source: if a dm-verbatim list placed the butter one rank higher, the value would move to `high`.
limitations: A soft preference with a stated reason, never an exclusion.

careDirection.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–12; comparative care emphasis, never an assertion about a user's protein state (G6).
careDirection.rationale: CHANGED under v0.2 (R6). The two-readings rule deletes the lipid-leg path into `balanced`: a protein-led formula whose only other leg is lipid breadth now reads `protein`, which is what its architecture says. The protein leg leads and there is no qualifying humectant cluster beside it. v0.1 recorded this value as reached 'by the letter' of a test whose bar it judged too low; R6 raises the bar and the value follows. E2 ceiling: comparative emphasis, not a delivered outcome.
evidenceSignals: HYDROLYZED SILK (rank 11) — qualifying R5 hydrolyzed protein above the tail (PARFUM @13)
SERICIN (rank 12) — second distinct qualifying R5 species above the tail; lexicon family 5a names sericin explicitly

GLYCERIN (rank 3) — the ONLY above-tail humectant. The §9.5.3 criterion-1 cluster (≥ 3 distinct, ≥ 2 non-glycerin) fails at one member, so the `moisture` leg does not lead and `balanced` reading (a) is unavailable
ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE (6) + GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS (10) — the S3 lipid breadth that carried v0.1's `balanced`. Under R6 this path is deleted: generic lipids are what every rich mask carries

HYDROXYPROPYLGLUCONAMIDE (8) / HYDROXYPROPYLAMMONIUM GLUCONATE (9) — deliberately NOT counted here (§6 rule 4: the bond token may set repair_support_level or corroborate the repair focus, but the same token cannot also be a protein-film route for care_direction)
careDirection.derivation: §9.3 (R6). Material R5 test, leg (a): two distinct qualifying R5 species above the tail — HYDROLYZED SILK @11 and SERICIN @12. Leg (b) not reached (neither is within the first eight above-tail ranks). `balanced` reading (a) requires the material R5 route AND a qualifying humectant cluster: the cluster fails at one member. `balanced` reading (b) requires NO protein anchor (clause 1) and fails immediately. Therefore the protein leg leads with no qualifying humectant cluster beside it → `protein`.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `protein`: a material identifiable R5 film-support route that is more than ordinary conditioning, with no qualifying humectant cluster beside it.
`balanced` (a) both-substantive does not apply: only one humectant above the tail.
`balanced` (b) neither-dominant does not apply: clause 1 requires no protein anchor, and there is one.
`moisture` does not apply: it is the coherent direction WITHOUT a material protein-film route, and a two-species R5 route above the tail is one.

R6's cohort effect is visible here exactly as ruled: 'protein + generic lipids' no longer reaches `balanced`. This is the first `protein` value produced anywhere in the cohort — under v0.1 the field's `protein` bucket was empty across all twelve products, which the v0 run flagged as likely structural unreachability.

Re-checked under v0.4 (E8, 2026-09-30): value `protein` STANDS. The one hinge this record flagged (AP-04-R5TAILEDGE) is ruled: a tail_index − 1 species counts normally in §9.3, exactly as E1 rules for §9.1/§9.2, with the dependence recorded as a confidence cap and a hinweise note.
counterSignals: D4 heavy-protein-payload counter-signal FIRES (two distinct R5 species above the tail): confidence bound to `moderate` (§13 effect 2), carried in `hinweise` as `protein_payload` (§13.1, R8), and routed under `protein_payload_review`.

BOUNDARY POSITION (E8, 2026-09-30): the material R5 route rests on HYDROLYZED SILK @11 plus SERICIN @12, and SERICIN sits at tail_index − 1 (PARFUM @13). E8 rules that R3's tail-edge exclusion is not extended to §9.3's material-R5 test: following E1, the species counts normally and the dependence costs confidence, not credit. SERICIN is load-bearing — without it HYDROLYZED SILK @11 stands alone, leg (b) fails (not within the first eight above-tail ranks), and the value would be `moisture` — so confidence is capped at `moderate` (already bound there by D4) and a `boundary_position_ingredient` note is emitted.
The humectant leg is a single glycerin — a category base ingredient whose rank carries no moisture signal at all (lexicon family 7).
limitations: INCI discloses no molecular weight; the R5 route supports 'a protein film route is present' and nothing more (P-5 is entirely MW-conditional).
Banned vocabulary observed: no 'protein overload', 'Proteinüberschuss', 'protein-sensitive hair' or 'protein break' language anywhere in this record.

repairSupportLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only; a deterministic gate on a named INCI token, expressing comparative formula potential — never efficacy.
repairSupportLevel.rationale: The canonical gluconamide pair is declared above the tail marker, which is the sole route to `high` under §9.4. R7's standing caveat is carried in full: no bond route has strong independent product-level substantiation at drugstore concentrations, and gluconamide bonding's own peer-reviewed literature (Cryst. Growth Des. 2022) explicitly states that the mechanism by which the mixture affects hair is unknown, proposing hydrogen-bonded salt bridges only as a hypothesis. This value gates a comparative formula-potential reading, not a claim that the product repairs anything.
evidenceSignals: HYDROXYPROPYLGLUCONAMIDE (rank 8) — above tail_index 13
HYDROXYPROPYLAMMONIUM GLUCONATE (rank 9) — above tail_index 13; lexicon family 6 requires the pair, and the pair is present
HYDROLYZED SILK (11) + SERICIN (12) — an independent qualifying R5 route that would have earned `medium` on its own
repairSupportLevel.derivation: §9.4: `high` requires bond_route ≠ none. bond_route = gluconamide on the named-token test, both members above the tail. No further condition applies.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `high`: the deterministic gate is met by the exact token pair lexicon family 6 names as the canonical positive, at ranks 8 and 9 against a marker at 13.
`medium` does not apply as the final value, though it is independently earned: the two-species R5 route above the tail would give `medium` even with no bond route. `high` supersedes it.
`low` does not apply: two independent qualifying routes are present.

Explicit non-upgraders checked and none relied upon: Amodimethicone @14 is an amino silicone and is BOTH a listed non-qualifier and in the tail; Lactic Acid @16 is the amidoamine neutraliser (C3), never bond evidence; Glycosphingolipids @10 is a ceramide-class species and an explicit family-6 non-qualifier.
counterSignals: Confidence is capped at `moderate` rather than `high` because §9.4 requires a VERIFIED exact-market INCI for high confidence, and this list rests on a single fallback-tier source with both preferred retailers unreachable. The token identification itself is unambiguous.
Nothing in the exact-product positioning ('HaptIQ System & Seide', 'Bonding') was used to reach this value; the route was determined blind.
limitations: Banned wording observed: no 'repairs', 'rebuilds bonds', 'restores structure', or 'reverses damage'.
§18 open question 7 is answered affirmatively by this product: the qualifying gluconamide tokens CAN be pinned exactly, so the enum value is as deterministic here as `maleate` would be.

primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2 mechanism grouping: the bond pair is one M2-adjacent observation, the silk/sericin pair is an M2 observation, and the cationic/lipid base is one M1 observation — three separable groups. Step 3, first route tested: `repair` requires a distinct R5 protein/peptide film route OR R7 named bond chemistry. Both are present. The hierarchy stops at step 3 for the primary slot.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `repair`: §9.5.2 step 3's requirement is disjunctive and both disjuncts are independently satisfied.

`shine` does not apply, and this is the product's key discrimination: despite 'Liquid Silk Glanz' front-of-pack, §9.5.4 criterion 1 requires an alignment-oriented R2/R3 route ABOVE the tail, and the formula's only silicone (Amodimethicone) is at rank 14, one rank below the marker, with no cationic polymer anywhere. Criterion 1 fails outright, so criterion 3's claim corroboration is never reached. Positioning cannot create the route (step 9).
`moisture` does not apply: it is tested after repair and would fail its own guard anyway (Glycerin @3 is the sole above-tail humectant against a required three).

Re-checked under v0.2 (R5, R7). The `repair` headline is unaffected: it rests on the named gluconamide pair above the tail (bond_route `gluconamide`), not on a moisture/repair tie. R5's lipid-led disqualifier is not reached, because the `moisture` route never cleared criterion 1 — GLYCERIN @3 is the only above-tail humectant. R7's tie-break is not reached either: the verdict is `repair_supported`, not `dual_supported`, and R7 permits a tie-break only on a genuinely dual verdict.
counterSignals: §6 rule 4 was observed: the bond token sets repair_support_level and corroborates the repair focus, but was not additionally counted as the protein-film route for care_direction — the silk/sericin pair carried that independently.
Confidence `moderate`, not `high`, because both legs rest on a single fallback-tier transcription and the R5 leg sits at the boundary band.
limitations: R7 standing caveat carried into the focus rationale: 'Bond' front-of-pack is frequently an ordinary rich mask, and this product's qualifying route is architecture evidence, not efficacy.

focusCareVerdict.note: A coherent substantive damage-care cluster supports repair — not merely one protein token: a named bond pair at ranks 8/9 plus two distinct hydrolyzed protein species at 11/12, all above the marker. The 'Bonding' positioning corroborates a route that was already earned blind; it neither created nor broke a tie. The 'Glanz'/'Liquid Silk' half of the positioning was refused corroborating force entirely, because §9.5.4 criterion 1 failed before criterion 3 was reachable.

adjudicationPoints.title: CLOSED by E8 (2026-09-30) — the tail-edge exclusion does not reach §9.3; SERICIN @12 counts and care_direction stays `protein` at moderate confidence
adjudicationPoints.body: Raised under v0.2: `care_direction: protein` rests on a two-species material R5 route, HYDROLYZED SILK @11 + SERICIN @12, and SERICIN sits exactly at tail_index − 1 (PARFUM @13). The point asked whether R3's tail-edge exclusion reached §9.3's material-R5 test; if it did, the value would fall to `moisture`. E1 (2026-09-14) withdrew the exclusion everywhere and made the boundary treatment field-uniform; Nick confirmed the §9.3 half explicitly as E8 on 2026-09-30: the exclusion is NOT extended to the protein test, a tail_index − 1 species counts normally there, and the boundary dependence is recorded as confidence capped at `moderate` plus a `boundary_position_ingredient` hinweise note (now emitted). The value stays `protein`. The bond route (@8/@9) was never in the band, so `repair_support_level: high` and the `repair` headline were unaffected in either reading. Nothing further is needed from Nick on this record.
